compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a scheduling meeting, two people may both ask whether the same criteria were applied to each option. That illustrates the shared Thinking preference, although a job requirement could also explain the question.

E/I describes the direction of attention and energy. S/N describes the kinds of information a person tends to give weight to. J/P describes how a person approaches structure and open options in the outside world. None measures how rational someone is.

### ESTJ and INTP: the same changeover meeting, different things checked

In this fictional example, two planners have the same authority, staffing limits, and deadline. Both can review the time window, staffing, and parts. Comparable records can support a workable plan, but assumptions still need checking. Exploring alternatives can reveal weak assumptions, but the team still needs a plan it can use.

The planners have three changeovers to schedule and only an aggregate time from last season. One approach checks which measured times and documented constraints apply this week. Another asks whether differences in tooling or trial runs could explain the figure and affect the schedule. The example illustrates attention to concrete evidence and possible patterns.

Either planner can use both approaches. Authority, responsibilities, time, and missing information affect which question is most urgent. The order of those questions does not identify ESTJ or INTP.

### ESTJ and INTP: three letters apart, two names overlapping

In type dynamics, the J in ESTJ indicates that its outward-facing process is a judging process: dominant extraverted Thinking (Te), paired with auxiliary introverted Sensing (Si). For INTP, the P indicates an outward-facing perceiving process: auxiliary extraverted Intuition (Ne), paired with dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). In this notation, ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi and INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe.

Si and Ne are the only shared processes with the same attitude in this notation, switching the auxiliary and tertiary positions. Both stacks show Feeling in the fourth position, with different attitudes (Fi and Fe). These positions describe the model and do not predict the order of anyone’s actions.

The Foundation’s overview lists tertiary Intuition for ESTJ (Ne or Ni) and tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si). This page uses Ne and Si. Those alternatives leave the first two positions unchanged. compare_blocks.body:
The fictional situations below illustrate how people review information and communicate. Workplace procedures and authorized staff govern quality and release decisions. Qualified professionals handle construction safety.

### ESTJ and INTP: who fixes the window and who lists the assumptions

In this fictional changeover meeting, the person authorized to make commitments owns the customer date. The person with access to the measurements documents the assumptions. These responsibilities can go to either type or to the same person.

Document the estimates, which steps depend on them, and when they need to be checked. The timing depends on what the schedule needs. A deadline does not make an unverified estimate more reliable.

For the delivery review, record which figures the team relied on, which assumptions still need checking, and who can make the decision. This record helps review the plan and cannot identify type.

### ESTJ and INTP: planning a bathroom renovation for a parent

In this fictional example, two siblings review the same estimates for grab bars and slip-resistant flooring. One line of inquiry concerns costs, timing, and how they will know the work is complete. Another concerns what a qualified contractor needs to verify before recommending an installation. Either sibling can ask both sets of questions.

Cost and timing affect when the work can happen. The contractor’s findings help the family understand whether the proposed work addresses their concerns. The family can ask what is still uncertain and what the contractor will check when the work is complete.

An ESTJ can ask about installation standards and an INTP can negotiate a quote. Those questions do not reveal how much either person cares or identify their type. Structural and electrical decisions belong to qualified professionals.

One person may focus on the documented batch and who owns the follow-up. Another may ask whether the readings point to a measurement issue or a recurring pattern. Either person can ask both questions. These examples illustrate how to read the same record and offer no instructions for handling the part.

Who reviews what depends on training, authority, and the information available. A decision made under pressure cannot establish someone’s type.

comparison.summary:
ESTJ and INTP are two of the sixteen types, sharing only T and differing on E/I, S/N and J/P.

- **T (shared):** Thinking favors decisions based on principles and consistently applied criteria. People who prefer Thinking can still consider how a decision affects others.
- **E/I:** ESTJ has a preference for Extraversion, which directs attention and energy more toward the outer world. INTP has a preference for Introversion, which directs them more toward inner ideas and reflection. Speaking time does not identify either preference.
- **S/N:** ESTJ has a preference for Sensing, emphasizing observable details and relevant experience. INTP has a preference for Intuition, emphasizing connections, patterns, and possibilities.
- **J/P:** ESTJ has a preference for Judging, which favors structure and closure in dealings with the outside world. INTP has a preference for Perceiving, which favors keeping options open to new information.
- **Cognitive functions:** In the notation used here, ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi and INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe. They share Si and Ne, with the auxiliary and tertiary positions reversed. Sources differ on the tertiary process’s attitude. The stacks describe preferences within a model. Sending a spreadsheet or asking a question first cannot identify a type.

compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
All six examples use the same records, staffing limits, decision authority, and delivery deadline. Either person can give weight to the same evidence or adopt the same plan.

| Same situation, information, and authority | ESTJ: possible emphasis | INTP: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Making sense of the same plan | Attention may turn outward toward the exchange with colleagues and their feedback | Attention may turn inward toward reflecting on the same questions | E/I: orientation of attention and energy. Either person can discuss the plan or reflect privately. |
| Only last season’s aggregate time is available | What the records actually measured and which figures are estimates | What patterns in the same records might explain the total and point to missing information | S/N: documented details versus possible connections |
| A faster sequence is proposed | What the shift records and parts lead times show about the affected steps | How the proposed sequence could shift delays between those same steps | S/N: documented constraints versus possible consequences across the plan |
| Closing the scheduling meeting | Set a provisional window and review point within approved limits | Keep eligible windows open until the same pending measurement arrives | J/P: forming an outward arrangement versus retaining options. Both can use either approach. |
| Planning a crew briefing | Choose a provisional time and format while keeping the approved instructions | Keep several times or formats open under the same approved instructions | J/P: settling a provisional arrangement versus keeping options available |
| Reviewing the same record of a first-part deviation | What the part measured and which batch and inspection the result came from | Whether those same records show a recurring deviation and which explanations remain possible | S/N: individual measurements versus a pattern to verify. The approved procedure governs handling. |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a scheduling meeting, two people may both ask whether the same criteria were applied to each option. That illustrates the shared Thinking preference, although a job requirement could also explain the question.

E/I describes the direction of attention and energy. S/N describes the kinds of information a person tends to give weight to. J/P describes how a person approaches structure and open options in the outside world. None measures how rational someone is.

### ESTJ and INTP: the same changeover meeting, different things checked

In this fictional example, two planners have the same authority, staffing limits, and deadline. Both can review the time window, staffing, and parts. Comparable records can support a workable plan, but assumptions still need checking. Exploring alternatives can reveal weak assumptions, but the team still needs a plan it can use.

The planners have three changeovers to schedule and only an aggregate time from last season. One approach checks which measured times and documented constraints apply this week. Another asks whether differences in tooling or trial runs could explain the figure and affect the schedule. The example illustrates attention to concrete evidence and possible patterns.

Either planner can use both approaches. Authority, responsibilities, time, and missing information affect which question is most urgent. The order of those questions does not identify ESTJ or INTP.

### ESTJ and INTP: three letters apart, two names overlapping

In type dynamics, the J in ESTJ indicates that its outward-facing process is a judging process: dominant extraverted Thinking (Te), paired with auxiliary introverted Sensing (Si). For INTP, the P indicates an outward-facing perceiving process: auxiliary extraverted Intuition (Ne), paired with dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). In this notation, ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi and INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe.

Si and Ne are the only shared processes with the same attitude in this notation, switching the auxiliary and tertiary positions. Both stacks show Feeling in the fourth position, with different attitudes (Fi and Fe). These positions describe the model and do not predict the order of anyone’s actions.

The Foundation’s overview lists tertiary Intuition for ESTJ (Ne or Ni) and tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si). This page uses Ne and Si. Those alternatives leave the first two positions unchanged. See the [ESTJ profile](/en/personality/estj) and the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) for the full preference descriptions.
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
The fictional situations below illustrate how people review information and communicate. Workplace procedures and authorized staff govern quality and release decisions. Qualified professionals handle construction safety.

### ESTJ and INTP: who fixes the window and who lists the assumptions

In this fictional changeover meeting, the person authorized to make commitments owns the customer date. The person with access to the measurements documents the assumptions. These responsibilities can go to either type or to the same person.

Document the estimates, which steps depend on them, and when they need to be checked. The timing depends on what the schedule needs. A deadline does not make an unverified estimate more reliable.

For the delivery review, record which figures the team relied on, which assumptions still need checking, and who can make the decision. This record helps review the plan and cannot identify type.

### ESTJ and INTP: planning a bathroom renovation for a parent

In this fictional example, two siblings review the same estimates for grab bars and slip-resistant flooring. One line of inquiry concerns costs, timing, and how they will know the work is complete. Another concerns what a qualified contractor needs to verify before recommending an installation. Either sibling can ask both sets of questions.

Cost and timing affect when the work can happen. The contractor’s findings help the family understand whether the proposed work addresses their concerns. The family can ask what is still uncertain and what the contractor will check when the work is complete.

An ESTJ can ask about installation standards and an INTP can negotiate a quote. Those questions do not reveal how much either person cares or identify their type. Structural and electrical decisions belong to qualified professionals.

### ESTJ and INTP: the first part out of tolerance at two in the morning

In this fictional example, a first-part measurement is outside tolerance. Both people have the same inspection record and work under the same approved procedure. The procedure and authorized personnel govern decisions about the line, further inspection, notifications, and release.

One person may focus on the documented batch and who owns the follow-up. Another may ask whether the readings point to a measurement issue or a recurring pattern. Either person can ask both questions. These examples illustrate how to read the same record and offer no instructions for handling the part.

Who reviews what depends on training, authority, and the information available. A decision made under pressure cannot establish someone’s type.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
Bluntness and warmth do not identify a Thinking preference. Either type can apply consistent criteria and consider how a decision affects a colleague.

Speed depends on the work, the evidence, and the deadline. An INTP can act quickly on a familiar problem, and an ESTJ can revisit a procedure when it stops working.

A job title, technical skill, or qualification does not establish a type. Te and Ti describe different orientations of Thinking within the model. Neither measures someone’s ability to manage a team or do technical work.

ESTJ and INTP share Thinking even though three letters differ. In this notation, Si and Ne also appear in both stacks. Both types can draw on experience and consider new possibilities.

faq_blocks.answer:
E/I, S/N and J/P; only T is shared.

E/I concerns outward or inward attention and energy. S/N concerns concrete experience or patterns and possibilities. J/P concerns structure or open options in outward-facing matters. The model represents ESTJ as Te–Si–Ne–Fi and INTP as Ti–Ne–Si–Fe under the convention used here. None of the three differences can be inferred from who acted first.
faq_blocks.question: Which three letters do ESTJ and INTP differ on?

faq_blocks.answer:
In the notation used here, Si and Ne switch between the auxiliary and tertiary positions. Te and Ti are dominant, while Fi and Fe occupy the inferior positions.

The Foundation allows more than one attitude for the tertiary process. The comparison uses Ne for ESTJ and Si for INTP. The positions describe the model and do not predict who speaks first or who is more attentive to relationships.
faq_blocks.question: The stacks overlap on only two names — what does that mean?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. An ESTJ can revise a schedule when the data, constraints, or applicable procedure changes.

An INTP can keep a schedule when its assumptions still hold. Either person can communicate who is affected, what is changing, and what the team needs to review.
faq_blocks.question: Does an ESTJ also overturn a schedule just issued?

faq_blocks.answer:
A scheduling role can require making a plan workable across several teams and checking the assumptions behind it. Review whether the staffing and timing fit, whether the records support the estimate, and who can approve the plan.

Either person may have to coordinate the work or test the schedule. To reflect on preferences, compare several similar situations where you had a choice. Job performance and wording in a status report cannot establish type.
faq_blocks.question: What should both types check in a scheduling role?

faq_blocks.answer:
A schedule can already be circulating while some assumptions remain open. Either person might emphasize protecting commitments or checking new evidence. The team needs to address both concerns.

Define who can confirm an external date, which assumptions remain provisional, and how approved changes will reach the crews. Use the organization’s timetable and procedures to decide when changes can be made.
faq_blocks.question: What can cause friction when ESTJ and INTP work together?

faq_blocks.answer:
Compare the instrument, version, language, and scoring guidance. Consider whether you were answering about your usual preferences or about what your job requires.

Use the instrument’s reporting guidance if it gives interpretable scores for each preference pair. A change in labels alone cannot show whether a score was close to the cutoff or why it changed.

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
In a scheduling meeting, two people may both ask whether the same criteria were applied to each option. That illustrates the shared Thinking preference, although a job requirement could also explain the question.

E/I describes the direction of attention and energy. S/N describes the kinds of information a person tends to give weight to. J/P describes how a person approaches structure and open options in the outside world. None measures how rational someone is.

### ESTJ and INTP: the same changeover meeting, different things checked

In this fictional example, two planners have the same authority, staffing limits, and deadline. Both can review the time window, staffing, and parts. Comparable records can support a workable plan, but assumptions still need checking. Exploring alternatives can reveal weak assumptions, but the team still needs a plan it can use.

The planners have three changeovers to schedule and only an aggregate time from last season. One approach checks which measured times and documented constraints apply this week. Another asks whether differences in tooling or trial runs could explain the figure and affect the schedule. The example illustrates attention to concrete evidence and possible patterns.

Either planner can use both approaches. Authority, responsibilities, time, and missing information affect which question is most urgent. The order of those questions does not identify ESTJ or INTP.

### ESTJ and INTP: three letters apart, two names overlapping

In type dynamics, the J in ESTJ indicates that its outward-facing process is a judging process: dominant extraverted Thinking (Te), paired with auxiliary introverted Sensing (Si). For INTP, the P indicates an outward-facing perceiving process: auxiliary extraverted Intuition (Ne), paired with dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). In this notation, ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi and INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe.

Si and Ne are the only shared processes with the same attitude in this notation, switching the auxiliary and tertiary positions. Both stacks show Feeling in the fourth position, with different attitudes (Fi and Fe). These positions describe the model and do not predict the order of anyone’s actions.

The Foundation’s overview lists tertiary Intuition for ESTJ (Ne or Ni) and tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si). This page uses Ne and Si. Those alternatives leave the first two positions unchanged. See the [ESTJ profile](/en/personality/estj) and the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) for the full preference descriptions.

| Same situation, information, and authority | ESTJ: possible emphasis | INTP: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |

| Making sense of the same plan | Attention may turn outward toward the exchange with colleagues and their feedback | Attention may turn inward toward reflecting on the same questions | E/I: orientation of attention and energy. Either person can discuss the plan or reflect privately. |

sections.title: ESTJ and INTP in one minute

sections.body_md:
The fictional situations below illustrate how people review information and communicate. Workplace procedures and authorized staff govern quality and release decisions. Qualified professionals handle construction safety.

### ESTJ and INTP: who fixes the window and who lists the assumptions

In this fictional changeover meeting, the person authorized to make commitments owns the customer date. The person with access to the measurements documents the assumptions. These responsibilities can go to either type or to the same person.

Document the estimates, which steps depend on them, and when they need to be checked. The timing depends on what the schedule needs. A deadline does not make an unverified estimate more reliable.

For the delivery review, record which figures the team relied on, which assumptions still need checking, and who can make the decision. This record helps review the plan and cannot identify type.

### ESTJ and INTP: planning a bathroom renovation for a parent

In this fictional example, two siblings review the same estimates for grab bars and slip-resistant flooring. One line of inquiry concerns costs, timing, and how they will know the work is complete. Another concerns what a qualified contractor needs to verify before recommending an installation. Either sibling can ask both sets of questions.

Cost and timing affect when the work can happen. The contractor’s findings help the family understand whether the proposed work addresses their concerns. The family can ask what is still uncertain and what the contractor will check when the work is complete.

An ESTJ can ask about installation standards and an INTP can negotiate a quote. Those questions do not reveal how much either person cares or identify their type. Structural and electrical decisions belong to qualified professionals.

### ESTJ and INTP: the first part out of tolerance at two in the morning

In this fictional example, a first-part measurement is outside tolerance. Both people have the same inspection record and work under the same approved procedure. The procedure and authorized personnel govern decisions about the line, further inspection, notifications, and release.

One person may focus on the documented batch and who owns the follow-up. Another may ask whether the readings point to a measurement issue or a recurring pattern. Either person can ask both questions. These examples illustrate how to read the same record and offer no instructions for handling the part.

Who reviews what depends on training, authority, and the information available. A decision made under pressure cannot establish someone’s type.
sections.title: ESTJ and INTP at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
Bluntness and warmth do not identify a Thinking preference. Either type can apply consistent criteria and consider how a decision affects a colleague.

Speed depends on the work, the evidence, and the deadline. An INTP can act quickly on a familiar problem, and an ESTJ can revisit a procedure when it stops working.

A job title, technical skill, or qualification does not establish a type. Te and Ti describe different orientations of Thinking within the model. Neither measures someone’s ability to manage a team or do technical work.

ESTJ and INTP share Thinking even though three letters differ. In this notation, Si and Ne also appear in both stacks. Both types can draw on experience and consider new possibilities.

sections.body_md:
If two results differ, compare the instrument, version, language, and scoring. Consider whether you answered with your usual preferences in mind or the demands of a job. Those demands can affect which examples come to mind without establishing a direction for the score change.

If a score sits near a boundary, interpret it against that tool's scoring and reporting notes; one borderline reading, or two results that differ, cannot establish the cause — it may be item coverage, the situation you answered in, or the tool's own scoring.

Recall several decisions with similar responsibilities and deadlines where you had a genuine choice. Record the information you relied on, how you weighed it, and whether you settled the outward arrangement or kept options open. Recurring themes can help you reflect. This exercise cannot determine a type.

E/I, S/N and J/P; only T is shared.

E/I concerns outward or inward attention and energy. S/N concerns concrete experience or patterns and possibilities. J/P concerns structure or open options in outward-facing matters. items.question: Which three letters do ESTJ and INTP differ on?

items.answer:
In the notation used here, Si and Ne switch between the auxiliary and tertiary positions. Te and Ti are dominant, while Fi and Fe occupy the inferior positions.

The Foundation allows more than one attitude for the tertiary process. The comparison uses Ne for ESTJ and Si for INTP. The positions describe the model and do not predict who speaks first or who is more attentive to relationships.
items.question: The stacks overlap on only two names — what does that mean?

items.answer:
Yes. An ESTJ can revise a schedule when the data, constraints, or applicable procedure changes.

An INTP can keep a schedule when its assumptions still hold. Either person can communicate who is affected, what is changing, and what the team needs to review.
items.question: Does an ESTJ also overturn a schedule just issued?

items.answer:
A scheduling role can require making a plan workable across several teams and checking the assumptions behind it. Review whether the staffing and timing fit, whether the records support the estimate, and who can approve the plan.

Either person may have to coordinate the work or test the schedule. To reflect on preferences, compare several similar situations where you had a choice. Job performance and wording in a status report cannot establish type.
items.question: What should both types check in a scheduling role?

items.answer:
A schedule can already be circulating while some assumptions remain open. Either person might emphasize protecting commitments or checking new evidence. The team needs to address both concerns.

Define who can confirm an external date, which assumptions remain provisional, and how approved changes will reach the crews. Use the organization’s timetable and procedures to decide when changes can be made.
